drills.q: Why does a CNN need dramatically fewer parameters than an MLP for the same image input?
drills.a: Parameter sharing: the same kernel (e.g. 1792 params for a 3x3 conv, 3->64 channels) is convolved at every spatial position, independent of image size. A dense layer on a flattened image needs a separate weight per input-position/unit pair -- over 100x more for a 32x32x3 image to 64 units.

drills.q: Derive the output spatial size of a 32x32 input through a 3x3 kernel, stride 1, padding 1.
drills.a: H' = floor((H-K+2P)/S)+1 = floor((32-3+2)/1)+1 = 32 -- spatial size preserved ('same' padding).

drills.q: What is receptive field and how much does one additional 3x3 stride-1 conv layer add to it?
drills.a: How much of the input a feature-map location depends on. RF(L layers) = 1+2L for 3x3 stride-1 layers -- 5 layers give RF=11, 10 layers give RF=21.

drills.q: Explain why BPTT is not a separate algorithm from ordinary backpropagation.
drills.a: Unrolling an RNN across T timesteps gives an ordinary computation graph where the same weights are reused (tied) at every timestep. BPTT is reverse-mode AD applied to this weight-tied graph, with the shared weight's gradient accumulated across all T timesteps, following the same rule any reused parameter gets.

drills.q: Why does a vanilla RNN suffer vanishing gradients across long sequences, in mechanical terms?
drills.a: The unrolled graph is structurally a T-layer deep network with tanh activations (derivative ceiling below 1) repeated every timestep -- the identical product-of-derivatives vanishing-gradient argument, with sequence length T playing the role of depth L.

drills.q: Write the four LSTM gate equations and the cell-state and hidden-state updates.
drills.a: f_t=sigmoid(Wf.[h,x]+bf), i_t=sigmoid(Wi.[h,x]+bi), g_t=tanh(Wg.[h,x]+bg), o_t=sigmoid(Wo.[h,x]+bo). c_t = f_t*c_{t-1} + i_t*g_t. h_t = o_t*tanh(c_t).

drills.q: Why does the LSTM's additive cell-state update specifically fix vanishing gradients?
drills.a: d(c_t)/d(c_{t-1}) = f_t, a single learned factor the network can keep near 1 for persisting information, rather than a forced product of weight Jacobian and saturating activation derivative -- the 'constant error carousel', mechanically the same fix idea as a residual connection's I+Jf Jacobian.

drills.q: Are LSTMs fully immune to vanishing or exploding gradients? Explain.
drills.a: No -- the additive cell-state path resists vanishing specifically when the forget gate stays open, but the gates' own weight matrices and readout layers can still vanish or explode via the ordinary multiplicative mechanism, which is why gradient clipping remains standard for RNN/LSTM training.

drills.q: Why might you choose an LSTM over a Transformer in production in 2026?
drills.a: LSTM per-step inference cost is constant regardless of history length; attention's cost grows with context length (quadratic full attention or a growing KV cache). LSTMs can also generalize better in low-data regimes due to a stronger sequential inductive bias -- relevant for latency-constrained streaming or small-data tasks.

drills.q: Why does replacing Flatten->Dense with GlobalAveragePooling2D->Dense cut parameters so dramatically, and what does it cost?
drills.a: GAP averages each channel over its entire spatial extent, giving a C-length vector regardless of H,W, so the following dense layer scales with channel count not spatial size -- orders of magnitude fewer parameters. Cost: discards spatial position information, which matters for detection/segmentation but is fine for whole-image classification.

drills.q: What is Keras 3's key difference from pre-3.0 Keras, and what breaks its cross-backend portability?
drills.a: Keras 3 is multi-backend (TensorFlow, JAX, PyTorch, OpenVINO for inference) selected via KERAS_BACKEND. Using a raw backend-specific op (e.g. a tf.* call) instead of the backend-agnostic keras.ops.* API inside a model breaks that portability.

drills.q: Design: classifying fixed-length few-second audio clips into categories -- CNN or RNN/LSTM, and why? What changes if clips become minutes long with important info at arbitrary offsets?
drills.a: Short fixed clips, whole-clip classification: a 1D/2D CNN over the waveform/spectrogram is the pragmatic choice -- exploits local structure, trains with full parallelism, doesn't need unbounded-range modeling. For minute-long clips with arbitrary-offset relevant info, attention-based architectures become more competitive since they give direct access to any time offset without the receptive-field-growth cost of stacking more conv layers.
